claim: A routine made faster must be padded back to the original duration or the saving credited, or the game speeds up and pace moves with the work done.

evidence.text: The first sprite fast path made the game run 14% fast in the simulator (7.41 frames an update against 8.59); its saving is added back to the wait (spr_credit), giving 8.47.
evidence.quote: The sprite fast path's saving is added back to D (spr_credit) so the pace stays the original's: without it the simulator's pace ran 14% fast (7.41 frames an update against 8.59).

evidence.text: Hooks that replace a plot rather than add to it need the plot's original time back in the wait, or pace still moves with the plot count.
evidence.quote: Hooks that replace a plot rather than add to it need the plot's original time back in the wait (V_CR), or the pace still moves with the plot count.

evidence.text: A room at 28 MHz needs its original time back: a fit over all rooms, then a wait at the game's clock.
evidence.quote: A room at 28 MHz needs its original time back: a fit over all rooms, then a wait at the game's clock

evidence.text: The cheapest honest pace fix is a wrapper: halt to the frame interrupt, then draw at 28 MHz (NextReg 0x07 = 3) inside the frame.
evidence.quote: the cheapest honest pace fix is the wrapper `pace_wrapper(call)`: halt to the frame interrupt, draw at 28 MHz (NextReg 0x07 = 3) inside the vertical
